chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The foundling (child) is neither bought nor sold.

key_terms.اللَّقِيطُ: Foundling; a child whose parents are unknown and is found abandoned.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a foundling child in Shia fiqh regarding sale and purchase?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that a 'laqeet' (foundling) cannot be bought or sold, distinguishing their status from chattel slaves in early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling, transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurara, underscores the foundling's inherent human dignity and right to maintenance, preventing their commodification in the marketplace. It reflects the broader Shia legal principle that while a foundling may be possessed for care, their core identity remains distinct from property.
